doc.title: Abe Most interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, February 13, 1999

title: State of studio work, Local 47 and the contractors
summary: The RMA, top contractors, and why calls have dried up, so he plays tributes to Goodman and Shaw.

story.theme_name: Radio and television work: staff jobs, shows and broadcasts
story.community_name: Studio work and jingles: New York session life

blocks.x: Now this, you mentioned that he used a lot less people than the standard orchestra. Where is the status of the orchestra these days now in the film studios?

There are still, let me say it this way. In the union there are about, I used to think there was 10,000 but I think it’s about half, it’s about 5,000 let’s say. Of that there’s a group called RMA, Recording Musician’s Association, which I am not a member of ‘cause I don’t do that much work anymore. If I did I’d probably belong to it. Because those people, and there are only about, let me back up. The RMA has about 1,100 members within the union, Local 47, and that’s 1,100 out of 5,000, even 6,000. That’s a very small group. The 5,000 on the outside do all the casuals, places like this hotel, private parties, and like that. But in the RMA they have the motion pictures, T.V., recordings and theater, all the high profile jobs. And only about 300 I would say of the RMA make a good living. All the others are peripheral, like maybe once in a while they’ll get a call. So it’s boiled down to if you’re in that select group, and if you’re called by Sandy DeCrescent, who is the top contractor in town, or Patty, well she used to be DeCarrol, Patti Zimmitti, another contractor, and there are two or three other lesser lights. But those two are the main contractors and if you get a call from them, you’re in, if they start calling you. Well they stopped calling me a while back, maybe it’s my gray hair, I don’t know. You know when your contractors and leaders don’t ask for you then — so I’m just facing reality in that nobody knows Abe Most within the theater realm of things, and I’m now doing like a Tribute to Benny Goodman and Tribute to Artie Shaw, and whatever. way. And occasional calls. I have a call, I do some commercials and a few pictures, and once in a while, I don’t know what this one is coming up, I have something in a couple of weeks. In the meantime I do some jazz gigs or something. Luckily, busy enough.
